pass_condition: Every 06 section 4 row field the store declares is actually produceable by some write path.

findings.statement: stars_audited is in 06 section 4's row contract but round 2 removed the only path that could set it: the writer hardcodes NULL and no parameter accepts a value.
findings.quoted_line: None,  # stars_audited: no producer yet (see module docstring)
findings.failure_scenario: get_row returns stars_audited None for a fully-populated rated write. Round 1 took it from TieBreakInput.stars; RepoWrite(record, bundle) has no stars anywhere, and FeatureBundle/RepoIdentity carry none, so W4-4's leaderboard and W4-5's UI will render an empty column with no packet owning the gap.

observations: Verified there is genuinely no v2 producer: RepoIdentity has no stars/forks field and no GateEvidence class carries one; the only trace is cvi/derive/bundle.py:1056 reading provenance for 'stars'/'forks' out of the v1 shape. So round 2's NULL is more honest than round 1's caller-injected number -- the gap is real and needs an owner, not a writer argument.

Columns NULL on a fully-populated rated write: stars_audited, forks, last_human_commit_at, deep_dive_json (plus the correctly-NULL gate_reason/routed/unrated_reason/tier_ceiling/rank/tie_group for that fixture).

last_human_commit_at has the same shape and is already named in the writer docstring and in cvi.core.tiebreak's; deep_dive_json is unchanged from round 1 and still has no consumer in 06 section 4 or 04 section 7.
The packet documents all three in a test (test_stars_forks_last_commit_are_null_no_producer), which is the right disclosure.
